newVisited.ore: Photography is explicitly framed as representation, desire/projection, the collapse of objective safe viewing, and a reversal of gaze: the photographed world looks back.

newVisited.title: Chp 3_M20160309.docx
newVisited.ore: Amsterdam Red Light District material links micro-spatial form (alley/canal/window), visibility, intimacy, safety, rent, property value and redevelopment. Spatial configuration is treated as an active mechanism that redistributes economic value and power rather than as passive background.

leads.summary: A later visual-text layer carries the older representation problem into photography: objective appearance is treated as a screen for desire, while the object of vision can return the gaze. Candidate bridge between urban representation research and later image work; do not yet unify them.

The Amsterdam chapter exposes a concrete mechanism: tiny differences in spatial form and visibility change interaction, safety, rental prices, property value and redevelopment outcomes. Candidate ore for a recurring question about how spatial arrangements manufacture value and social relations.

speculative: The 2020 photography text may be a media migration of the earlier representation/symptom problem: from 'city as imperfect representation' to 'photograph as non-objective representation that looks back'. This is only a mining lead, not a conclusion.

The 2016 Amsterdam window material may intersect the value-form seam without using the same theoretical language: geometry/visibility becomes rent and redevelopment value. Keep separate until more layers are mined.
